intro: Agglomerative clustering builds a hierarchy one merge at a time. Single linkage measures two groups by their nearest pair of members.
task: Choose the closest cluster pair and update the distance matrix for one single-linkage merge.
requirements: distances is a square symmetric nonnegative matrix of size k>=2, with diagonal zero and symmetry tolerance 1e-10.
Choose the smallest off-diagonal distance; exact ties choose the lexicographically first (i,j) with i<j. Merge j into i and remove row and column j.
Return {"pair": integer array [i,j], "distance": merge_distance, "distances": new matrix}. Merged distances are min(old[i,c],old[j,c]); retain the order of surviving clusters.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Scan the upper triangle in row order to choose the earliest pair among exact distance ties.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Only distances involving the merged group change; use the smaller of its two previous connections.

explanation: Single linkage needs only the smallest connection between clusters. After a merge, the nearest connection to a third group must have come from one of the two old groups.
The pair uses original indices while the new matrix retains the order of surviving rows. Removing one cluster does not change distances between two untouched clusters.
